'0.4 This standard is intended to be used with the rolloving series of Indian Standards on plastics for, food contact applications: 13:9845-1981 Methods of analysis for the determination of specific and/or overall migration of constituents of plastics materials and articl~s intended to come into contact with foodstuffs; rS:10141-1982 Positive list of constituents of polyethylene in contact with foodstuffs, pharmaceuticals and drinking water; rS:lOl42-1982 Specification for styrene polymers for its safe use in contact with foodstuffs, pharmaceuticals and Jrinking vater; rS:lOl46-1982 Specification for polyethylene for its safe use in contact with foodstuffs, pharmaceuticals and drinking water; rS:lOl48-l982 Positive list of constituents of polyvinyl chloride (PVC) and its copolymers in contact with foodstuffs, pharmaceuticals and drinking water;

O.

FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 5 March 1981, after the draft finalized by the Plasncs Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. 0.2 The packaging of foodstuffs and pharmaceuticals is essential for their conservation, transport and handling. It also avoids contarnmarion and maintains hygienic conditions. There" always a possibIlity of transfer of part of packaging matertal to the packed matenial due to intimate contact of each other. Therefore, formulation 01 the packaging material must be selected to ensure that any such transfer is at a minimum and substances which do migrate f,om package to the packed material cause no toxic hazard on consumption. These considerations are equally important in case of processing equipment and utensils which come 10 contact with food, pharmaceuticals, etc. 0.3 This standard is expected serve as a basic guide on the constitution of the plastics with regard to their colouring matters whicb are considered toxicologically safe and not on tbe manner of their actual processing or use. The list of pigments and coJourants prescr-ibed in this standard IS based on the information available through published literature of the French Regulation and other naeronal legislarion reports. The toxicological effects of these colourants have not been investigated so far. 0.3.1 In this standard, limits for copper and ti" have not been prescribed as copper and tin are not released from metallic pigments to toxic Iimirs.

1. SCOPE 1.1 Thrs standard lis.. permitted pigments and colourants for use with plastics and may be regarded as safe for use In contact wi.h food, pharmaceuticals and drlnkmg water.

2. REQUIREMENTS
2.1 PIgments or colourants used shall not show visible bleeding or migration from the fimshed product and shall show no signs of instability or degradation during processing. 2.2 Pigments and cotourante used sball have a high degree of purity. In particular, if the following impurities are present these shall not exceed the hmit specified below. a) Lead, percent by mass, Max b) Arsenic, percent by mass, Max
